name: Freshwater marsh
notes: Treeless emergent wetland on mineral soil with standing fresh water: tall stands of cattail, reed and bulrush grade into sedge tussocks, iris and sweet-grass at the margins with scattered willow/sweet-gale; drawn on the North American prairie potholes and Great Lakes marshes and the European reedbeds (Danube, Norfolk Broads).

shrub.name: Grey willow
shrub.source: Salix cinerea, grey willow, Europe & W Asia, willow carr invading fen and marsh margins, 3-7 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

shrub.name: Sweet gale
shrub.source: Myrica gale, bog myrtle, circumboreal, scented shrub of marsh and fen margins, 0.6-2 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

shrub.name: Buttonbush
shrub.source: Cephalanthus occidentalis, buttonbush, eastern North America, shrub of marsh edges standing in shallow water, 1.5-4 m, white ball flowers — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

ground.name: Cattail
ground.source: Typha latifolia, broadleaf cattail, circumboreal (N America, Eurasia), dominant emergent of freshwater marsh, 1.5-3 m, brown sausage heads — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

ground.name: Common reed
ground.source: Phragmites australis, common reed, cosmopolitan, vast reedbeds in freshwater and brackish marsh, 2-4 m feathery plumes — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Soft-stem bulrush
ground.source: Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani, softstem bulrush, cosmopolitan, leafless round culms in shallow open water of marshes, 1-3 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

ground.name: Yellow flag iris
ground.source: Iris pseudacorus, yellow flag, Europe, W Asia & N Africa, marsh margins and ditches, 0.7-1.5 m sword leaves, yellow flowers — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Tussock sedge
ground.source: Carex stricta, tussock sedge, eastern & central North America, dense tussocks in sedge meadows and marsh edges, 0.5-1.2 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

ground.name: Reed sweet-grass
ground.source: Glyceria maxima, reed sweet-grass, Europe & W Asia, lush stands on nutrient-rich marsh and river margins, 1-2.5 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

special.note: Catalogue plants (data/plants) whose band centres fall inside this biome's climate; computed, informational. Phase 6 may raise their density here so they are findable.

associations.name: Cattail-bulrush deep marsh
associations.where: standing water most of the year, mineral mud, open basin center
associations.source: Prairie pothole deep-marsh zone (Stewart & Kantrud 1971; USNVC)

associations.name: Common reed bed
associations.where: shallow water and wet basin margins, sheltered, silty
associations.source: Phragmition reedswamp (Ellenberg 1988; Rodwell 1995 British Plant Communities S4)

associations.name: Tussock sedge meadow
associations.where: seasonally flooded outer margin, saturated but rarely deep
associations.source: Carex stricta sedge meadow (Curtis 1959 Vegetation of Wisconsin; USNVC)

associations.name: Willow-buttonbush marsh edge
associations.where: shrubby marsh margin and drainage lines, waterlogged soil
associations.source: Shrub-carr and buttonbush swamp (Curtis 1959; Rodwell 1991 W1 Salix cinerea woodland)
